title: Safety and benefit of discontinuing statin therapy in the setting of advanced, life-limiting illness: a randomized clinical trial
authors: Kutner JS, Blatchford PJ, Taylor DH, Ritchie CS, Bull JH, Fairclough DL, et al.
followUp: up to 1 year; primary end point at 60 days
population: Adults with an estimated life expectancy of 1 month to 1 year, statin therapy for 3 months or more for primary or secondary prevention, recent functional decline and no recent active cardiovascular disease; mean age 74.1 years, 48.8% with cancer
funder: This study received funding from the National Institute of Nursing Research (grants UC4-NR012584 and U24-NR014637), with resources and facilities of the Veterans Affairs Health Care System. The National Institute of Nursing Research had no role in the design and conduct of the study; collection, management, analysis, and interpretation of the data; preparation, review, or approval of the manuscript; and decision to submit the manuscript for publication.
result: Unblinded pragmatic trial: 189 participants were randomised to discontinue and 192 to continue statins. Death within 60 days: 45 (23.8%) after discontinuation against 39 (20.3%) with continuation (90% CI of the difference -3.5% to 10.5%; P = 0.36); non-inferiority was not achieved because the upper limit exceeded the prespecified margin of 5%. Median time to death 229 against 190 days (P = 0.60). Cardiovascular events in 13 against 11 participants. Mean total McGill quality-of-life score (0 to 10, area under the curve) 7.11 against 6.85 (P = 0.04). The primary end point was changed from survival to death within 60 days partway through the trial on the advice of the data and safety monitoring board.
